title: [finding] three sibling list doors carry the same declared-but-never-read `limit`/`cursor` shape that #17667 is retiring on `/packages` — export jobs, AI conversations and automation runs
body:
Path: none | 清单区 api-backend:列表门的分页 | 三扇兄弟门声明 `limit`/`cursor` 却从不读,其一还带 `.default(20)` 让读声明的客户端以为有上限

Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 3 (`session_01HnRAeVTLJevtQ5iCPX6JSm`), ⏱️ 2026-09-20T13:40Z, from the `out_of_scope_findings` of the `os-dev` delivering **#17667** (report on that card). ⛔ Not triaged, ⛔ no `domain:*`, ⛔ no priority — routing and grading are the triage seat's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The defect

**#17667** is retiring `limit` and `cursor` from `ListInstalledPackagesRequestSchema` because the `/packages` list door **declares them and never reads them** — a caller that asks for one row is handed the whole table alongside a `hasMore: false` that agrees with it.

⭐ **Three sibling doors carry the identical shape**, and #17667 names none of them:

| schema | declared | read |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ListExportJobsRequestSchema` | `limit` with **`.default(20)`**, `cursor` | no |
| `ListAiConversationsRequestSchema` | `limit`, `cursor` | no |
| `ListRunsRequestSchema` | `limit`, `cursor` | no |

⇒ `.default(20)` on the first is the same trap `.default(50)` was on `/packages`: a declared-schema reader (an SDK, codegen, an **AI client**) is entitled to believe an unparameterised list is capped, and it is not capped at all.

## ⭐ The automation door states the gap in its own comment

`GET /automation/:name/runs` **validates `cursor` at the boundary** and then returns `{ runs, hasMore: false }`, with its own comment recording that 「today's engine ignores the option entirely」. ⇒ the door performs the ceremony of accepting a pagination parameter and then discards it — the declared contract and the enforced behaviour disagree **in the source's own words**.

## Repro

Same as #17667's: against any host serving these domains with more than one row, ask any of the three for one row or for a second page. You are handed the full set with `hasMore: false`. Nothing in the status, headers or body distinguishes that from a request served as asked.

## Class

**(b) — violates an already-declared contract.** The request schema is the declaration; the handler is the enforcement; they disagree.

⭐ **The decision shape is already precedented, so this should be cheap**: ruling `5651023067` (decision batch #126 item 1, maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-13) settled exactly this question for `/packages` — **route 2**, align the declaration with what the door executes; route 1 (implement paging) and route 3 (refuse unknown params) were considered and refused. ⛔ That ruling governs `/packages` only; whether it extends to these three is a judgement this card exists to put, ⛔ not one this seat makes.

⚠️ Note for whoever grades it: **#17667 deliberately did not widen onto these**, and that was correct — the ruling named one door. This card is the successor, ⛔ not a criticism of that scope.

## Dedupe words

`list door declared limit` · `cursor never read` · `hasMore hard-coded false` · `export jobs pagination declared` · `automation runs cursor ignored`
